contexts.text: Therefore the feast of tabernacles was instituted. AC 3312:end. AC 4391:end. AC 10545:2. AR 585:end. AE 724:16.
Therefore the feast of seven Sabbaths was on the fiftieth day.
The feast of tabernacles = holy worship, thus worship from good and truth.

And hold a feast to Me in the wilderness () = that from a glad mind they may worship the Lord in the obscurity of faith in which they are. To hold a feast = worship from a glad mind... because the feast was to be held at a way of three days from Egypt, thus in a state of no infestation by falsities: that is, in a state of freedom... Moreover the feasts which were instituted among that people, which were three in the year, are said to have been instituted in memory of deliverance from slavery in Egypt; that is, in a spiritual sense, in memory of deliverance from infestation by falsities by the advent of the Lord into the world. Illustrated. AC 7882.
Because it is a feast of Jehovah to us () = the worship of the Lord in each and all things.
The reason no work was to be done on the feasts and Sabbaths...
But afterwards the same feasts were retained for the sake of heavenly life on those occasions, and for the sake of doctrine, that they might then learn what faith and charity are.
On the seventh day a feast to Jehovah () = the holy worship of the Lord.
They have no feast days.
See Feast.

The feast of unleavened things = purification from falsities; the feast of harvest, the implantation of truth in good; and the feast of ingathering, the implantation of the good thence derived... AC 9287. AC 9294. AC 9294:2. AC 9295. AC 9296. AC 9296:4. AC 9296:5. AC 10670. AC 10671. AC 10671:2.
Therefore the three feasts in the year also = worship of the Lord and thanksgiving on account of regeneration. AC 9294:2.
These three feasts are also called the feast of the passover, the feast of weeks, and the feast of tabernacles. Illustrated.
Like things to those represented by these three feasts, are represented by...
As by this second feast, which is called the feast of the first-fruits of works, and also the feast of weeks...

As by the third feast, which was called the feast of the ingathering of the fruits of the earth, and of the ingathering from the threshing-floor and the winepress; and also the feast of tabernacles...

(Thus) the three feasts were instituted on account of the bringing forth of the human race, who are willing to receive new life from the Lord, out of Hell, and their introduction into Heaven; and this by the Lord through His advent into the world.
Feast = worship.
The dung of feasts () = the defilement of the holy things of worship.
Afterwards was instituted the feast of tents...
A feast of Jehovah tomorrow ()... A feast = the worship of the Church as to celebration; for on feast days a celebration took place.
Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened things () = worship of the Lord and thanksgiving on account of deliverance from evil and falsities of evil.
As to this feast, it properly = the glorification of the Lord's Human, thus the remembrance thereof, and thanksgiving on that account...
The Lord has provided that in every religion... a festival is to be observed.
(Heaven supposed to be a continuous festival.)
On Spirits who were celebrating a feast of tabernacles.
The feast of tabernacles = the implantation of the good of celestial love, or of love.
To bind the feast to the horns of the altar () = to conjoin together all things of worship... Feast, and altar = worship.
Feast = worship. AE 433:11. AE 601:end. AE 706:21. AE 863:2.
As the feast of tabernacles = the implantation of good through truths...
That they had completely destroyed all things of Divine worship, is signified by their having burnt all the festal places of God ().
The three feasts = the whole of regeneration, from first to last...

As such things are signified by harvest, there were two feasts instituted among the Israelites; one called the feast of weeks, which was that of the firstfruits of the harvest; and the other the feast of tabernacles, which was that of the ingathering of the fruits of the earth; and of which the former = the implantation of truth in good, and the latter, the production of good, thus regeneration: but the feast of unleavened things, or of the Passover, which preceded them, = deliverance from falsities of evil, which is the first of regeneration.
Therefore they were glad in the feasts...
